concept_purpose: Aesthetic category theorizing how performative labor and frantic affect under post-Fordist capitalism becomes a comic style; 'zany' names the precarious worker stretched across too many roles
paper_title: A Precarious and Zany Youth: The Feminist Comedy of Malena Pichot
paper_argument: Reads Malena Pichot's web series Cualca through Ngai's zaniness to show how feminist comedy registers the generalized precarity and misogyny of the Argentine media-labor context, pushing against postfeminist representation

concept_purpose: Affective condition of living in chronic instability under neoliberalism, where the promise of the good life frays into ongoing crisis ordinariness
paper_title: A Precarious and Zany Youth: The Feminist Comedy of Malena Pichot
paper_argument: Uses precarity to argue that Pichot's comedy both depicts and is produced within precarious labor structures, making feminist politics inseparable from the economics of online cultural production

concept_purpose: Concept describing the commodified management of feelings demanded of workers, especially women, as part of the job under service capitalism
paper_title: Post-#MeToo Reflections on Pre-#MeToo TV Production: Female Actors' Precarity, Agency, and Emotional Labor
paper_argument: Argues that female TV actors performed extensive emotional labor and navigated precarity and constrained agency within pre-#MeToo production cultures, reframing on-set abuse as a structural labor problem

concept_purpose: Concept for how platform infrastructures, data and business models reorganize the production and circulation of cultural goods and creative labor
paper_title: Losing Color Consciousness: Platformization and Precarious Practices in Premiere Pro
paper_argument: Argues that the platformization of editing software like Adobe Premiere Pro embeds precarious, deskilled color-grading practices, eroding craft knowledge ('color consciousness') among media workers

concept_purpose: Framework for the 'somebodies/nobodies' divide produced as generative AI manufactures digital performers, restructuring consent, identity and labor value of human performers
paper_title: 'Somebodies' and 'Nobodies': Generative AI and Audiovisual Performer Labor
paper_argument: Argues generative AI splits performers into valued 'somebodies' and disposable 'nobodies', intensifying precarity and raising ethical questions of consent and identity manipulation in synthetic media labor

theorist: Robert E. Weems / Robert L. Allen
concept_purpose: Critical concept analyzing the postwar incorporation of Black economic advancement into corporate and consumer capitalism as a containment of radical Black politics
paper_title: Help (1970): Afram and Black Capitalism
paper_argument: Reads the corporate-sponsored film Help (1970) and the Afram organization as artifacts of black capitalism, showing how media promoted entrepreneurial uplift as a response to civil-rights-era demands

concept_purpose: Performative theory of assembly: bodies gathering in public enact a plural, embodied politics that exceeds speech, grounding claims to appear and to live a livable life
paper_title: Crowd Choreographies: Spike Lee's BlacKkKlansman (2018) and the Politics of (Post)Cinematic Assembly
paper_argument: Reads BlacKkKlansman's crowd scenes through Butler's performative assembly to theorize how cinema choreographs collective bodies, articulating a politics of (post)cinematic assembly across affect and montage

concept_purpose: Theory of laughter (Le rire) as a social corrective: laughter is inherently collective, an élan that disciplines mechanical rigidity and binds the group
paper_title: 'The Most Revolutionary Affect of the Masses': Collective Laughter
paper_argument: Mobilizes Bergson on contagious laughter to argue that hysterical collective laughter is a revolutionary mass affect blurring anxiety and enjoyment, theorizing bodily contagion as political potential

concept_purpose: Theory of the masses and distraction: the modern collective body absorbs technological media reception, opening laughter and shock as politicized mass experience
paper_title: 'The Most Revolutionary Affect of the Masses': Collective Laughter
paper_argument: Draws on Benjamin's account of the masses to read viral and historical instances of collective laughter as a revolutionary affect of the technologically mediated crowd

concept_purpose: Concept of fabulation / 'the people to come': minor cinema invents a missing people through legending rather than representing an existing collective
paper_title: Fabulation, Magical Transformation, and Montage: Reconsidering the Complex Correspondences between Cinema and the People
paper_argument: Reconsiders Deleuze's fabulation and the people-to-come to rethink how montage and magical transformation in cinema relate to 'the people', proposing a richer model of cinema-collectivity correspondence

concept_purpose: Deconstructive critique of sovereignty: the spectral, non-self-present basis of democracy ('democracy to come') that troubles the autonomous sovereign subject and nation
paper_title: The Beekeeper's Ghost: Democracy and Transsovereignty in Zanny Begg's The Beehive
paper_argument: Theorizes 'transsovereignty' via the figure of the beehive and the spectral to argue that Begg's The Beehive stages a democracy haunted by and exceeding bounded sovereignty

concept_purpose: Concept of governmentality: the rationalities and techniques (the 'conduct of conduct') through which modern states administer populations beyond direct coercion
paper_title: Institutional Film and Social Public Policies in Portugal during the Late Authoritarian Regime (1957-1969)
paper_argument: Analyzes the Junta de Acção Social's institutional films as instruments of a corporatist governmentality, showing how the Estado Novo used cinema to mold social public policy on work and education

concept_purpose: Anticolonial theory of revolutionary violence and Third-World solidarity that framed 1960s Italian left reception of decolonization aesthetics
paper_title: When Violence Appeals: The Circulation and Reception of Brazilian Cinema Novo in Italy (1960-1968)
paper_argument: Argues that Italian festivals and left-wing critics received Cinema Novo through emergent third-worldist theory, shaping its canonization while reproducing uneven North-South power relations

concept_purpose: Historical-materialist reception study: meanings of films are produced in concrete contexts of exhibition and criticism, and canons are constructed through these reception practices
paper_title: When Violence Appeals: The Circulation and Reception of Brazilian Cinema Novo in Italy (1960-1968)
paper_argument: Historicizes the early Italian reception of Cinema Novo at festivals and in journals to show how critical reception practices forged its canonical international status

concept_purpose: Transnational and entanglement frameworks reconceiving early cinema across shifting national borders rather than within fixed nation-states
paper_title: Thessaloniki in Early Cinema History: Cinematic Entanglements and Disentanglements amid Moving Borders in the Balkans and the Eastern Mediterranean
paper_argument: Uses entanglement/transnational frameworks to write Thessaloniki's early cinema history through moving Balkan borders, decentering national cinema historiography

concept_purpose: Critique of la technique: technology develops by its own self-augmenting logic, an autonomous imperative that subordinates social and political choice
paper_title: Fossil Fuel Infrastructure in the 1920s: US Bureau of Mines Films and the Technological Imperative
paper_argument: Argues that 1920s US Bureau of Mines films naturalized fossil-fuel infrastructure as a technological imperative, using government film to render extractive industry inevitable and progressive

concept_purpose: Theory of useful/sponsored cinema: non-theatrical films made to do organizational work (instruct, persuade, govern) rather than to entertain
paper_title: The American Landscape and the New Deal in Art and Film
paper_argument: Reads New Deal government landscape films as useful/sponsored cinema that aestheticized state policy, linking documentary form to art-historical traditions of the American landscape

concept_purpose: Infrastructure studies of media distribution: the material networks (16mm, satellites, depots) that move films and structure access and power
paper_title: Entertainment Spanning the Universe: Movies at War, Free Films, and the US Military's 16mm Distribution Infrastructure
paper_argument: Reconstructs the US military's 16mm distribution infrastructure to show how the apparatus of free-film circulation built wartime morale and exported American entertainment globally

concept_purpose: Theory that memory is socially framed: groups construct and reconstruct a shared past through institutions and media to serve present needs
paper_title: Ending the Erbfeindschaft: Neighbors (1963), a West German Governmental PR Film, and the Manipulation of Collective Memory in the Context of the Elysee Treaty
paper_argument: Argues that the West German PR film Neighbors (1963) manipulated Franco-German collective memory to reframe 'hereditary enemies' as friends in the service of Elysee Treaty reconciliation

concept_purpose: Concept of elemental media (water, air, fire, infrastructure as media): natural environments and milieus understood as the basic media that condition existence
paper_title: Media-Milieu Dialectic: Thinking beyond Elemental Media
paper_argument: Critiques and extends Peters's elemental media by proposing a media-milieu dialectic, arguing the elemental must be thought together with the historically produced milieu rather than as a stable nature

concept_purpose: Deconstructive logic of the supplement: the 'add-on' that is also constitutive, exposing how form is never self-sufficient but structured by what it claims to merely extend
paper_title: The Queerness of Animation: Barry JC Purves and the Supplementarity of Form
paper_argument: Reads Purves's stop-motion animation through Derridean supplementarity to argue that animated form is constitutively queer, undoing norms of bodily and representational wholeness

concept_purpose: Theory of anachronism / survival (Nachleben): images carry heterogeneous times, so history is montage of non-contemporaneous moments rather than linear chronology
paper_title: Anachronic 1968: The Crisis of Media in Imagen de Caracas
paper_argument: Uses anachronism to read the multimedia spectacle Imagen de Caracas as an 'anachronic 1968', theorizing the work's crisis of media as a montage of disjunctive revolutionary times

concept_purpose: Method of figural analysis: close attention to the figure (forms, bodies, plastic configurations) rather than narrative interpretation, an experimental rather than hermeneutic criticism
paper_title: Experiment, Never Interpret: Nicole Brenez and Figural Analysis
paper_argument: Expounds Brenez's figural analysis as a model that refuses interpretation in favor of experimentation, arguing for an avant-garde practice of reading film images figurally

concept_purpose: Inquiry into why subjects obey: the affective and image-based mechanisms by which authority is rendered legitimate and disobedience becomes thinkable
paper_title: Why Obey?
paper_argument: A translated essay theorizing the question of obedience, examining how images and affects underwrite submission to authority and where the seeds of disobedience lie

concept_purpose: Phenomenology of the body and theory of gesture: meaning and politics are enacted through posture and bodily comportment, not only discourse
paper_title: Revolutionary Postures: Embodying Rupture in the Films of May 68
paper_argument: Reads films of May 68 through bodily posture and gesture to argue that revolutionary rupture is embodied and choreographed, locating politics in the comportment of filmed bodies

concept_purpose: Phenomenology of the racialized look: the Black subject is fixed and made hyper-visible/invisible by the white gaze, splitting body and being
paper_title: 'Those things you see through': Photography, Invisibility, and Blackness as Film in Jordan Peele's Get Out
paper_argument: Theorizes blackness as a photographic-cinematic condition of (in)visibility in Get Out, arguing the film stages how Black being is seen through, captured and rendered spectral by the racial gaze

concept_purpose: Critique of postfeminist sensibility: a media culture that recodes feminist gains into individualized, choice-and-empowerment rhetoric compatible with neoliberalism
paper_title: Hollywood, Reflexivity, and Barbarian: The Possibilities of Horror in the Wake of #MeToo
paper_argument: Argues the horror film Barbarian uses reflexivity to critique Hollywood's gendered abuses, reading post-#MeToo horror as exceeding postfeminist individualism toward systemic critique

concept_purpose: Theory of platform governance: moderation is the essential, value-laden product of platforms, defining acceptable speech and shaping public discourse
paper_title: How 'Cracker' Became 'Hate Speech': Content Moderation Logics and Right-Wing Mass Flagging on Twitch
paper_argument: Argues that Twitch's content-moderation logics are weaponized by right-wing mass-flagging campaigns, showing how governance infrastructures can be turned to reactionary ends

concept_purpose: Theory of networked self-presentation and 'context collapse': users perform calibrated, platform-legible selves for imagined audiences
paper_title: Performing Positive Energy: Mediated Self-Representation of Chinese Migrant Workers on Douyin
paper_argument: Argues Chinese migrant workers perform state-sanctioned 'positive energy' selves on Douyin, negotiating visibility within platform and ideological constraints

concept_purpose: Concept of the livable life: the social and material conditions (recognition, care, infrastructure) that make a life grievable and worth living, especially for precarious populations
paper_title: Trans+ Livability Politics: Euphoria's Mundane Spaces as Material Care
paper_argument: Reads Euphoria's mundane spaces as sites of material care, arguing the show stages a trans+ politics of livability grounded in everyday infrastructures of survival
